scenarios.title: Prepare a module for a different kernel
scenarios.summary: Recover missing per-kernel module installation from source registration and build records.
scenarios.objective: Install campus-net/1.4 for maintenance kernel 6.6.61. Preserve every supplied module record for running fallback kernel 6.6.60. No module-loading test is required or simulated.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the failing module/version/kernel row. Target the maintenance kernel explicitly; restore a changed fallback before retrying.

scenarios.explanation: Source registration makes a build-ready source available to DKMS. A build belongs to a particular kernel and architecture; it is not installed merely because compilation was recorded. An explicit -k selects the maintenance kernel, while an omitted -k selects the supplied running kernel. Installation may add/build as needed. The checks inspect actual installation records and independently compare the protected fallback.
hints: Read the supplied running kernel before choosing whether to omit -k. dkms status lists module/version, kernel, architecture and built/installed state.
Use the module/version and target kernel named in the requirements. Build is preparation; installed is placement.
Installation can add and build as needed; a separate add/build sequence is also valid.
scenarios.simplifications: Finite build-ready source/header fixtures, one architecture and one object per package. No C compilation, dkms.conf/Makefile evaluation, header/compiler/ABI failures, hooks, signing, original-module backups, automatic replacement, remove/autoinstall or actual module loading. Files and all DKMS commands are simulated. Different command forms and supported manual/chained operations are accepted by outcome.

scenarios.explanation: Module package versions can have independent build records for each kernel. In this disclosed subset, prepare the replacement, uninstall the older installed instance for the maintenance kernel, then install the replacement there. Uninstall retains its build and registration. Changing the target does not need to change the running fallback. Actual DKMS can also perform version sanity checks and automatic replacement; those additional behaviors are outside this exercise.
hints: Read the supplied running kernel before choosing whether to omit -k. dkms status lists module/version, kernel, architecture and built/installed state.
Use the module/version and target kernel named in the requirements. Build is preparation; installed is placement.
The supported handover uses an explicit uninstall of the old target instance, then installation of the replacement. Keep -k on both operations.
